---
title: "Brushless motors"
---

Background for [Module 2](/sessions/02-motor.qmd). For understanding why the motor behaves the way it
does when you push it in [Module 4](/sessions/04-control.qmd).

## Start with the brushed DC motor

Every result you need for a brushless motor is easier to see in a brushed one
first, because the two obey the same electrical physics. The difference is
*how* the windings get switched, not what the machine does once they are.

A DC motor is described by two constants and one resistance. Spinning the rotor
induces a back-EMF proportional to speed, and passing current through the
windings produces torque proportional to current:

$$U_\text{emf} = \frac{\omega}{k_V} \qquad\qquad \tau = k_T \, I$$ {#eq-two-constants}

These are the same $k_V$ and $k_T$ derived in
[Module 2](/sessions/02-motor.qmd) --- inverses of each other, not independent
choices. The supply voltage splits between the back-EMF and the ohmic drop
across the winding resistance $R$:

$$U = \frac{\omega}{k_V} + R \, I$$ {#eq-voltage-balance}

Substitute $I = \tau / k_T$ and rearrange for torque, and the whole behaviour
of the motor falls out as a **straight line**:

$$\tau = k_T \frac{U}{R} - \frac{k_T}{k_V R}\,\omega$$ {#eq-torque-speed}

### Reading the torque-speed line

That line is the motor's entire steady-state character, and it is fixed by the
applied voltage. Two points define it:

- **Stall torque** $\tau_\text{stall} = k_T U / R$, at $\omega = 0$. The rotor
  is held still, there is no back-EMF, and the only thing limiting current is
  the winding resistance. This is the largest torque the motor can produce and
  also the fastest way to destroy it - see [Thermal limits](#thermal-limits).
- **No-load speed** $\omega_0 = k_V U$, at $\tau = 0$. The rotor spins fast
  enough that the back-EMF nearly cancels the supply, so almost no current
  flows.

Everything the motor can do at that voltage lies on the line between them.
Mechanical power is $P = \tau \omega$, the product of a falling line and a
rising one, so it is a parabola peaking at **half the no-load speed** with half
the stall torque. Efficiency peaks somewhere else entirely --- much closer to
$\omega_0$, because the copper loss that dominates at low speed scales with
$I^2$ while the useful output only scales with $I$.

::: {.callout-note}
## The useful consequence

Raising the voltage shifts the line outwards without changing its slope: more
speed *and* more torque, same trade-off between them. That is why speed control
is voltage control, and why a "faster" motor at fixed voltage is a lower-torque
one.
:::

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}
<div class="viz" id="viz-volt"></div>
:::

::: {.content-visible unless-format="html"}
*(Online, this section carries a voltage slider showing the line sweeping
outwards.)*
:::

## What changes with a brushless motor

In a brushed motor the commutator and brushes are a mechanical switch riding on
the rotor: they physically reconnect the windings as it turns, so the current
always flows in whichever coil is best placed to produce torque. It works
without any electronics at all, and it wears out, arcs, and limits how fast the
motor can safely spin.

A **BLDC** motor deletes that switch. The permanent magnets go on the rotor,
the windings stay on the stator in three phases, and an external controller
decides which phases to energise based on where the rotor currently is. The
motor becomes inseparable from its driver --- this is why
[Module 3](/sessions/03-esc.qmd) exists, and why the rotor position measurement
matters so much.

What this does **not** change is @eq-torque-speed. The torque and speed
constants have the same meaning, the line has the same shape, and you size the
motor the same way. What changes is that the line is no longer the whole story:

| | Brushed | Brushless |
|---|---|---|
| Commutation | Mechanical, self-acting | Electronic, needs rotor position |
| Torque--speed line | The real limit | The *ideal* limit, then clipped by the driver |
| Wear | Brushes are consumable | Bearings only |
| Speed ceiling | Brush arcing and bounce | Commutation rate and sensor lag |
| Torque ripple | Smoothed by many commutator segments | Depends on drive scheme (trapezoidal vs FOC) |

### The envelope, not the line

The straight line assumes the supply can deliver whatever current the equations
ask for. It cannot. At stall, @eq-voltage-balance gives $I = U/R$, and with the
sub-ohm winding resistance of a small outrunner that is a number in the
hundreds of amps --- far beyond both the ESC and the motor itself.

So the driver enforces a **current limit**, and because $\tau = k_T I$ that is
directly a torque limit. The usable region becomes:

- a **constant-torque region** at low speed, flat at whatever current limit you
  set, because the ESC is holding current rather than letting the line dictate
  it;
- a **corner speed** where the back-EMF has risen enough that the supply can no
  longer push that current;
- above it, the original @eq-torque-speed line, falling to $\omega_0$.

The flat part is not physics, it is a decision. On our robot it is the decision
that keeps the motor alive at the low speeds used for swimming, where the
torque--speed line alone would happily draw enough current to cook the
windings.

## Thermal limits {#thermal-limits}

Nothing in @eq-torque-speed knows about heat, which is why the equations
cheerfully predict operating points that will destroy the motor in seconds.

Almost all the loss you care about is **copper loss** in the windings:

$$P_\text{copper} = I^2 R$$ {#eq-copper-loss}

The square is what makes this the binding constraint. Doubling the torque
doubles the current and **quadruples** the heating. A motor comfortable at
its rated current will not survive twice that for long, even though the torque
equation says it is only a factor of two.

Three practical consequences:

1. **Stall is the worst case, not the best.** At $\omega = 0$ there is maximum
   current and no rotation, so no airflow and no useful output --- all the
   input power becomes heat in the windings. A motor held at stall can burn out
   without the shaft moving at all.
2. **Continuous and peak ratings are different numbers.** A peak rating assumes
   seconds; a continuous rating assumes thermal equilibrium. Flapping is a
   *reciprocating* load, so the current is far from constant --- what matters
   for heating is the **RMS** current over the cycle, not the peak you see on
   the bench supply.
3. **Iron losses grow with speed.** Hysteresis and eddy-current losses in the
   stator scale with electrical frequency, so at the 1700 rad/s discussed in
   [Module 4](/sessions/04-control.qmd) the copper is no longer the only thing
   getting warm.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Heat is cumulative and invisible

Current is the only symptom you can see, and it appears instantly, while the
temperature it causes lags behind by tens of seconds. A run that looks fine on
the ammeter can still be depositing heat faster than the motor sheds it. When
tuning in [Module 4](/sessions/04-control.qmd), stop and touch the motor.
:::

## Why an outrunner

Brushless motors come in two arrangements. An **inrunner** spins a magnet rotor
inside a stationary stator, the familiar shape from a drill. An **outrunner**
inverts it: the stator sits still in the middle and the magnets are carried on
a bell that rotates around the outside. Ours is an outrunner --- it is the bell
you machine and press the shaft into in
[Module 2](/sessions/02-motor.qmd).

![An outrunner seen from the back. The copper windings are the **stator** and do not move; the dark magnet segments around the rim are carried on the rotating bell. Note how far out the magnets sit — that radius is the lever arm in @eq-torque-radius, and it is the whole reason for this arrangement. Note also that the heat is generated in the middle, wrapped inside the part that spins.](/Fig/motor.jpg){#fig-outrunner width="65%"}

The reason is torque. Torque is force times radius, and in an outrunner the
magnets sit at the *largest* radius the motor's diameter allows, rather than
the smallest:

$$\tau = F \times r$$ {#eq-torque-radius}

The same tangential force from the same windings acts on a longer lever arm. It
also leaves room for more magnet poles around the circumference. Together these
raise $k_T$ for a motor of the same mass, which by @eq-two-constants means a
**lower KV** --- more torque per amp, less speed per volt.

That is the right trade for us. The wings need torque at low speed, through a
gearbox that is already multiplying by 23.04:1, and the alternative is either a
larger reduction or more current for the same result. Two secondary properties
help as well:

- **Rotor inertia.** The rotating mass is at a large radius, so the bell has
  significant inertia and acts as a flywheel. Against a reciprocating flapping
  load that smooths the speed variation over a cycle. It also means the motor
  cannot change speed quickly, which is a real cost during transients.
- **Something to attach to.** The bell is a large-diameter rotating surface,
  which is what makes the shaft press-fit in
  [Module 2](/sessions/02-motor.qmd) mechanically sensible in the first place.

The costs are real: outrunners spin more slowly for a given voltage, the
exposed rotating bell is a hazard and an ingress path, and cooling is worse
because the heat-producing stator is wrapped inside the rotor rather than
mounted against the case. The last point ties directly back to
[Thermal limits](#thermal-limits) --- an outrunner's stator sheds heat mainly
through its mount, which on our robot is a 3D-printed plate.

<script>
(function () {
  "use strict";

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------
  // TEST-STAND DATA -- paste AS2303 measurements here.
  // One object per operating point:
  //   w      shaft speed          [rad/s]
  //   tau    measured torque      [mN.m]
  //   I      measured DC current  [A]   (optional)
  // Example:  { w: 420, tau: 38.5, I: 6.1 },
  // The final plot stays in its empty state while this array is empty.
  var MEASURED = [];

  // Motor parameters. KV is from the datasheet; R and I0 are PLACEHOLDERS
  // until the bench measurement lands -- see the instructor callout above.
  var KV = 1500;        // rpm/V
  var R_DEF = 0.06;     // ohm      PLACEHOLDER
  var I0_DEF = 0.9;     // A        PLACEHOLDER (no-load current)
  var U_DEF = 14.8;     // V        4S nominal

  var RPM2RAD = Math.PI / 30;
  var KT = 1 / (KV * RPM2RAD);          // N.m/A

  function model(U, R) {
    var w0 = KV * RPM2RAD * U;
    return {
      U: U, R: R, w0: w0,
      iStall: U / R,
      tStall: KT * U / R,
      cur: function (w) { return (U - KT * w) / R; },
      tau: function (w) { return KT * (U - KT * w) / R; },     // N.m
      pmech: function (w) { return w * KT * (U - KT * w) / R; }
    };
  }
  function effAt(m, w, i0) {
    var I = m.cur(w);
    if (I <= i0) return 0;
    return (KT * (I - i0) * w) / (m.U * I);
  }

  var NS = "http://www.w3.org/2000/svg";
  function mk(tag, attrs) {
    var e = document.createElementNS(NS, tag);
    for (var k in attrs) if (attrs[k] !== null) e.setAttribute(k, attrs[k]);
    return e;
  }
  function fmt(v, d) {
    return v.toLocaleString("en-US", { minimumFractionDigits: d, maximumFractionDigits: d });
  }
  function html(tag, cls, txt) {
    var e = document.createElement(tag);
    if (cls) e.className = cls;
    if (txt !== undefined) e.innerHTML = txt;
    return e;
  }

  // A single line panel with axes, gridlines, crosshair and tooltip.
  function Panel(host, opt) {
    var W = 720, H = opt.height || 210;
    var M = { t: 14, r: 78, b: 38, l: 62 };
    var iw = W - M.l - M.r, ih = H - M.t - M.b;
    var svg = mk("svg", { viewBox: "0 0 " + W + " " + H, role: "img",
                          "aria-label": opt.aria || opt.yLabel });
    host.appendChild(svg);

    var self = {
      svg: svg, W: W, H: H, M: M, iw: iw, ih: ih,
      xd: opt.xDomain, yd: opt.yDomain,
      x: function (v) { return M.l + (v - self.xd[0]) / (self.xd[1] - self.xd[0]) * iw; },
      y: function (v) { return M.t + ih - (v - self.yd[0]) / (self.yd[1] - self.yd[0]) * ih; },
      layers: {}
    };
    ["grid", "area", "line", "mark", "label", "hover"].forEach(function (n) {
      var g = mk("g", {}); svg.appendChild(g); self.layers[n] = g;
    });

    self.axes = function (xTicks, yTicks, xLabel, yLabel) {
      var g = self.layers.grid;
      while (g.firstChild) g.removeChild(g.firstChild);
      yTicks.forEach(function (t) {
        g.appendChild(mk("line", { x1: M.l, x2: M.l + iw, y1: self.y(t), y2: self.y(t),
                                   stroke: "var(--grid)", "stroke-width": 1 }));
        var lb = mk("text", { x: M.l - 8, y: self.y(t) + 4, "text-anchor": "end",
                              fill: "var(--muted)", "font-size": 11 });
        lb.textContent = opt.yFmt ? opt.yFmt(t) : t.toLocaleString("en-US");
        g.appendChild(lb);
      });
      xTicks.forEach(function (t) {
        var lb = mk("text", { x: self.x(t), y: M.t + ih + 17, "text-anchor": "middle",
                              fill: "var(--muted)", "font-size": 11 });
        lb.textContent = t.toLocaleString("en-US");
        g.appendChild(lb);
      });
      g.appendChild(mk("line", { x1: M.l, x2: M.l + iw, y1: M.t + ih, y2: M.t + ih,
                                 stroke: "var(--axis)", "stroke-width": 1 }));
      if (xLabel) {
        var xl = mk("text", { x: M.l + iw / 2, y: H - 2, "text-anchor": "middle",
                              fill: "var(--text-secondary)", "font-size": 11.5 });
        xl.textContent = xLabel; g.appendChild(xl);
      }
      if (yLabel) {
        var yl = mk("text", { x: 0, y: 0, "text-anchor": "middle", fill: "var(--text-secondary)",
                              "font-size": 11.5,
                              transform: "translate(13," + (M.t + ih / 2) + ") rotate(-90)" });
        yl.textContent = yLabel; g.appendChild(yl);
      }
    };

    self.path = function (pts, o) {
      o = o || {};
      var d = pts.map(function (p, i) {
        return (i ? "L" : "M") + self.x(p[0]).toFixed(2) + " " + self.y(p[1]).toFixed(2);
      }).join(" ");
      var el = mk("path", { d: d, fill: "none", stroke: o.stroke || "var(--s1)",
                            "stroke-width": o.width || 2, "stroke-linecap": "round",
                            "stroke-dasharray": o.dash || null, opacity: o.opacity || null });
      (o.layer ? self.layers[o.layer] : self.layers.line).appendChild(el);
      return el;
    };
    self.band = function (pts, y0, o) {
      var d = pts.map(function (p, i) {
        return (i ? "L" : "M") + self.x(p[0]).toFixed(2) + " " + self.y(p[1]).toFixed(2);
      }).join(" ");
      d += " L" + self.x(pts[pts.length - 1][0]).toFixed(2) + " " + self.y(y0).toFixed(2);
      d += " L" + self.x(pts[0][0]).toFixed(2) + " " + self.y(y0).toFixed(2) + " Z";
      self.layers.area.appendChild(mk("path", { d: d, fill: o.fill, opacity: o.opacity || 0.1,
                                                stroke: "none" }));
    };
    self.dot = function (px, py, o) {
      o = o || {};
      self.layers.mark.appendChild(mk("circle", { cx: self.x(px), cy: self.y(py), r: o.r || 4.5,
        fill: o.fill || "var(--s1)", stroke: "var(--surface-1)", "stroke-width": 2 }));
    };
    self.tag = function (px, py, text, color, anchor, dx, dy) {
      var t = mk("text", { x: self.x(px) + (dx || 0), y: self.y(py) + (dy || 0),
                           "text-anchor": anchor || "start", fill: color,
                           "font-size": 11.5, "font-weight": 600 });
      t.textContent = text;
      self.layers.label.appendChild(t);
    };
    self.clear = function () {
      ["area", "line", "mark", "label"].forEach(function (n) {
        var g = self.layers[n];
        while (g.firstChild) g.removeChild(g.firstChild);
      });
    };
    return self;
  }

  // Shared crosshair + tooltip across one or more panels sharing an x scale.
  function attachHover(container, panels, readout) {
    var tip = html("div", "viz-tip");
    container.appendChild(tip);
    panels.forEach(function (p) {
      var line = mk("line", { y1: p.M.t, y2: p.M.t + p.ih, stroke: "var(--muted)",
                              "stroke-width": 1, "stroke-dasharray": "3 3", opacity: 0 });
      p.layers.hover.appendChild(line);
      p.cross = line;
      var rect = mk("rect", { x: p.M.l, y: p.M.t, width: p.iw, height: p.ih,
                              fill: "transparent", style: "cursor:crosshair" });
      p.layers.hover.appendChild(rect);

      function move(ev) {
        var box = p.svg.getBoundingClientRect();
        var sx = (ev.clientX - box.left) / box.width * p.W;
        var xv = p.xd[0] + (sx - p.M.l) / p.iw * (p.xd[1] - p.xd[0]);
        xv = Math.max(p.xd[0], Math.min(p.xd[1], xv));
        panels.forEach(function (q) {
          q.cross.setAttribute("x1", q.x(xv));
          q.cross.setAttribute("x2", q.x(xv));
          q.cross.setAttribute("opacity", 1);
        });
        tip.innerHTML = readout(xv);
        tip.style.opacity = 1;
        var cbox = container.getBoundingClientRect();
        var left = ev.clientX - cbox.left + 14;
        if (left + tip.offsetWidth > cbox.width - 4) left = ev.clientX - cbox.left - tip.offsetWidth - 14;
        tip.style.left = Math.max(4, left) + "px";
        tip.style.top = (ev.clientY - cbox.top + 12) + "px";
      }
      function leave() {
        panels.forEach(function (q) { q.cross.setAttribute("opacity", 0); });
        tip.style.opacity = 0;
      }
      rect.addEventListener("pointermove", move);
      rect.addEventListener("pointerleave", leave);
    });
  }

  function ticks(lo, hi, n) {
    var out = [], step = (hi - lo) / n;
    for (var i = 0; i <= n; i++) out.push(Math.round((lo + i * step) * 100) / 100);
    return out;
  }
  // Round tick steps: 1, 2, 2.5, 3, 4, 5 or 10 times a power of ten.
  function niceStep(range, n) {
    var raw = range / n;
    var mag = Math.pow(10, Math.floor(Math.log(raw) / Math.LN10));
    var norm = raw / mag;
    var s = norm <= 1 ? 1 : norm <= 2 ? 2 : norm <= 2.5 ? 2.5
          : norm <= 3 ? 3 : norm <= 4 ? 4 : norm <= 5 ? 5 : 10;
    return s * mag;
  }
  function niceIn(max, n) {                 // ticks inside [0, max]; domain unchanged
    var st = niceStep(max, n), out = [];
    for (var v = 0; v <= max + st * 1e-9; v += st) out.push(Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6);
    return out;
  }
  function niceUp(max, n) {                 // round the domain top up to a tick
    var st = niceStep(max, n), top = Math.ceil(max / st - 1e-9) * st, out = [];
    for (var v = 0; v <= top + st * 1e-9; v += st) out.push(Math.round(v * 1e6) / 1e6);
    return { top: top, ticks: out };
  }
  function samples(m, n, f, wEnd) {
    var out = [], end = wEnd === undefined ? m.w0 : wEnd;
    for (var i = 0; i <= n; i++) { var w = end * i / n; out.push([w, f(w)]); }
    return out;
  }
  function legend(items) {
    var l = html("div", "viz-legend");
    items.forEach(function (it) {
      l.appendChild(html("span", null,
        '<i style="background:' + it.c + (it.dash ? ";height:0;border-top:2px dashed " + it.c : "") + '"></i>' + it.t));
    });
    return l;
  }
  function table(host, cols, rows) {
    var d = html("details");
    d.appendChild(html("summary", null, "Data table"));
    var t = html("table"), thead = html("tr");
    cols.forEach(function (c) { thead.appendChild(html("th", null, c)); });
    t.appendChild(thead);
    rows.forEach(function (r) {
      var tr = html("tr");
      r.forEach(function (c) { tr.appendChild(html("td", null, c)); });
      t.appendChild(tr);
    });
    d.appendChild(t);
    host.appendChild(d);
  }

  // ============================================================ 1. DC motor
  (function () {
    var host = document.getElementById("viz-dc");
    if (!host) return;
    var m = model(U_DEF, R_DEF), i0 = I0_DEF;

    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-title", "The three curves of a DC motor at fixed voltage"));
    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-sub",
      "Same motor, same " + U_DEF + "&nbsp;V supply, read three ways against shaft speed. " +
      "Torque falls in a straight line; power is their product, so it peaks in the middle; " +
      "efficiency peaks close to no-load. Hover to read all three at one speed."));

    var xT = niceIn(m.w0, 5);
    var pk = m.pmech(m.w0 / 2);
    // Efficiency is only defined while the motor still makes output torque,
    // i.e. while the total current exceeds the no-load current.
    var wEff = (m.U - i0 * m.R) / KT;
    var specs = [
      { yMax: m.tStall * 1000, lab: "Torque", unit: "mN·m", c: "var(--s1)", end: m.w0,
        f: function (w) { return m.tau(w) * 1000; } },
      { yMax: pk * 1.1, lab: "Power", unit: "W", c: "var(--s2)", end: m.w0,
        f: function (w) { return m.pmech(w); } },
      { yMax: 100, lab: "Efficiency", unit: "%", c: "var(--s3)", end: wEff,
        f: function (w) { return effAt(m, w, i0) * 100; } }
    ];
    var panels = specs.map(function (s, idx) {
      var ny = niceUp(s.yMax, 4);
      var p = Panel(host, { height: idx === 2 ? 190 : 165, yDomain: [0, ny.top],
                            xDomain: [0, m.w0], aria: s.lab + " against shaft speed" });
      p.axes(xT, ny.ticks, idx === 2 ? "Shaft speed ω [rad/s]" : null,
             s.lab + " [" + s.unit + "]");
      p.path(samples(m, 220, s.f, s.end), { stroke: s.c });
      return p;
    });
    // Direct labels on the features the text calls out.
    panels[0].dot(0, m.tStall * 1000, { fill: "var(--s1)" });
    panels[0].tag(0, m.tStall * 1000, "stall " + fmt(m.tStall * 1000, 0) + " mN·m",
                  "var(--s1)", "start", 8, 4);
    panels[1].dot(m.w0 / 2, pk, { fill: "var(--s2)" });
    panels[1].tag(m.w0 / 2, pk, "peak " + fmt(pk, 0) + " W at ω₀/2", "var(--s2)", "middle", 0, -10);
    var wBest = 0, eBest = 0;
    for (var i = 1; i < 400; i++) {
      var w = wEff * i / 400, e = effAt(m, w, i0);
      if (e > eBest) { eBest = e; wBest = w; }
    }
    panels[2].dot(wBest, eBest * 100, { fill: "var(--s3)" });
    panels[2].tag(wBest, eBest * 100, "peak " + fmt(eBest * 100, 0) + "%", "var(--s3)", "end", -9, 4);

    host.appendChild(legend([
      { c: "var(--s1)", t: "Torque" }, { c: "var(--s2)", t: "Power" }, { c: "var(--s3)", t: "Efficiency" }
    ]));
    attachHover(host, panels, function (w) {
      return "<b>" + fmt(w, 0) + " rad/s</b><br>Torque " + fmt(m.tau(w) * 1000, 0) +
             " mN·m<br>Current " + fmt(m.cur(w), 1) + " A<br>Power " + fmt(m.pmech(w), 0) +
             " W<br>Efficiency " + fmt(effAt(m, w, i0) * 100, 0) + "%";
    });
    table(host, ["ω [rad/s]", "Torque [mN·m]", "Current [A]", "Power [W]", "Eff [%]"],
      ticks(0, m.w0, 8).map(function (w) {
        return [fmt(w, 0), fmt(m.tau(w) * 1000, 0), fmt(m.cur(w), 1), fmt(m.pmech(w), 0),
                fmt(effAt(m, w, i0) * 100, 0)];
      }));
    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-note",
      "k<sub>V</sub> = " + KV + " rpm/V from the datasheet. R = " + R_DEF + "&nbsp;Ω and " +
      "no-load current I₀ = " + I0_DEF + "&nbsp;A are placeholders until the bench measurement " +
      "lands. The efficiency curve is the only one that uses I₀; without it the model would " +
      "predict 100% efficiency at no load."));
  })();

  // ======================================================== 2. Voltage slider
  (function () {
    var host = document.getElementById("viz-volt");
    if (!host) return;

    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-title", "What the supply voltage does to the line"));
    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-sub",
      "Drag the voltage. The line slides outwards and keeps its slope — the trade-off " +
      "between speed and torque never changes, only how much of both you get. " +
      "Grey lines mark 3S, 4S and 6S nominal for comparison."));

    var ctl = html("div", "viz-controls");
    var wrap = html("div", "viz-ctl");
    var lab = html("label", null, "Supply voltage <b>14.8 V</b>");
    var rng = html("input");
    rng.type = "range"; rng.min = 6; rng.max = 25.2; rng.step = 0.2; rng.value = U_DEF;
    rng.setAttribute("aria-label", "Supply voltage in volts");
    wrap.appendChild(lab); wrap.appendChild(rng); ctl.appendChild(wrap);
    host.appendChild(ctl);

    var stats = html("div", "viz-stats");
    var sDef = [["No-load speed", "rad/s"], ["Stall torque", "mN·m"],
                ["Stall current", "A"], ["Peak power", "W"]];
    var sEls = sDef.map(function (s) {
      var d = html("div", "viz-stat");
      d.appendChild(html("span", null, s[0] + " [" + s[1] + "]"));
      var b = html("b", null, "—");
      d.appendChild(b); stats.appendChild(d); return b;
    });
    host.appendChild(stats);

    var mMax = model(25.2, R_DEF);
    var nyV = niceUp(mMax.tStall * 1000, 4), xtV = niceIn(mMax.w0, 5);
    var p = Panel(host, { height: 250, xDomain: [0, mMax.w0], yDomain: [0, nyV.top],
                          aria: "Torque against speed for the selected supply voltage" });
    var cur = model(U_DEF, R_DEF);

    function draw() {
      var U = parseFloat(rng.value);
      cur = model(U, R_DEF);
      lab.innerHTML = "Supply voltage <b>" + fmt(U, 1) + " V</b>";
      p.clear();
      p.axes(xtV, nyV.ticks, "Shaft speed ω [rad/s]", "Torque [mN·m]");
      [11.1, 14.8, 22.2].forEach(function (u) {
        var r = model(u, R_DEF);
        p.path([[0, r.tStall * 1000], [r.w0, 0]], { stroke: "var(--muted)", width: 1.5, opacity: 0.45 });
      });
      p.band([[0, cur.tStall * 1000], [cur.w0, 0]], 0, { fill: "var(--s1)", opacity: 0.09 });
      p.path([[0, cur.tStall * 1000], [cur.w0, 0]], { stroke: "var(--s1)", width: 2.5 });
      p.dot(0, cur.tStall * 1000); p.dot(cur.w0, 0);
      p.tag(cur.w0, 0, fmt(U, 1) + " V", "var(--s1)", "start", 8, -4);
      sEls[0].textContent = fmt(cur.w0, 0);
      sEls[1].textContent = fmt(cur.tStall * 1000, 0);
      sEls[2].textContent = fmt(cur.iStall, 0);
      sEls[3].textContent = fmt(cur.pmech(cur.w0 / 2), 0);
    }
    rng.addEventListener("input", draw);
    draw();

    host.appendChild(legend([
      { c: "var(--s1)", t: "Selected voltage" },
      { c: "var(--muted)", t: "3S / 4S / 6S nominal" }
    ]));
    attachHover(host, [p], function (w) {
      if (w > cur.w0) return "<b>" + fmt(w, 0) + " rad/s</b><br>beyond no-load speed";
      return "<b>" + fmt(w, 0) + " rad/s</b><br>Torque " + fmt(cur.tau(w) * 1000, 0) +
             " mN·m<br>Current " + fmt(cur.cur(w), 1) + " A";
    });
    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-note",
      "Every line has the same slope — k<sub>T</sub><sup>2</sup>/R, set by the winding, " +
      "not by the supply. Raising the voltage moves both intercepts outwards together, which is " +
      "why stall current climbs just as fast as no-load speed does."));
  })();

  // ======================================================= 3. Thermal limits
  (function () {
    var host = document.getElementById("viz-thermal");
    if (!host) return;

    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-title", "Where the current limit cuts the line off"));
    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-sub",
      "The straight line assumes the supply will deliver whatever current the equation asks " +
      "for. The ESC will not. Set a limit and the usable region becomes a flat constant-torque " +
      "shelf, a corner speed, then the original line. The red band is everything above the " +
      "motor's continuous rating — survivable for seconds, not minutes."));

    var m = model(U_DEF, R_DEF);
    var ctl = html("div", "viz-controls");
    function slider(text, min, max, step, val, unit) {
      var w = html("div", "viz-ctl");
      var l = html("label", null, text + " <b>" + val + " " + unit + "</b>");
      var r = html("input");
      r.type = "range"; r.min = min; r.max = max; r.step = step; r.value = val;
      r.setAttribute("aria-label", text + " in " + unit);
      w.appendChild(l); w.appendChild(r); ctl.appendChild(w);
      return { r: r, l: l, text: text, unit: unit };
    }
    var sLim = slider("ESC current limit", 2, 60, 1, 20, "A");
    var sCon = slider("Motor continuous rating", 1, 30, 1, 10, "A");
    host.appendChild(ctl);

    var stats = html("div", "viz-stats");
    var sDef = [["Torque at limit", "mN·m"], ["Corner speed", "rad/s"],
                ["Copper loss at limit", "W"], ["Loss at continuous", "W"]];
    var sEls = sDef.map(function (s) {
      var d = html("div", "viz-stat");
      d.appendChild(html("span", null, s[0] + " [" + s[1] + "]"));
      var b = html("b", null, "—"); d.appendChild(b); stats.appendChild(d); return b;
    });
    host.appendChild(stats);

    var p = Panel(host, { height: 260, xDomain: [0, m.w0], yDomain: [0, 1],
                          aria: "Current-limited torque envelope against speed" });
    var state = { lim: 20, con: 10, yMax: 1 };

    function draw() {
      state.lim = parseFloat(sLim.r.value);
      state.con = Math.min(parseFloat(sCon.r.value), state.lim);
      sLim.l.innerHTML = sLim.text + " <b>" + state.lim + " A</b>";
      sCon.l.innerHTML = sCon.text + " <b>" + parseFloat(sCon.r.value) + " A</b>";

      var tLim = KT * state.lim * 1000, tCon = KT * state.con * 1000;
      var nyT = niceUp(tLim * 1.55, 4);
      state.yMax = nyT.top;
      p.yd = [0, state.yMax];
      p.clear();
      p.axes(niceIn(m.w0, 5), nyT.ticks, "Shaft speed ω [rad/s]", "Torque [mN·m]");

      // Above the continuous rating: heating faster than the motor sheds it.
      p.band([[0, state.yMax], [m.w0, state.yMax]], tCon,
             { fill: "var(--critical)", opacity: 0.09 });

      // Ideal line, mostly off the top of this scale.
      var wTop = (m.U - (state.yMax / 1000 / KT) * R_DEF) / KT;
      p.path([[Math.max(0, wTop), Math.min(m.tau(Math.max(0, wTop)) * 1000, state.yMax)],
              [m.w0, 0]], { stroke: "var(--s1)", width: 2, dash: "5 4" });

      // Current-limited envelope.
      var wCorner = (m.U - state.lim * R_DEF) / KT;
      var env = [[0, tLim], [wCorner, tLim]];
      for (var i = 1; i <= 40; i++) {
        var w = wCorner + (m.w0 - wCorner) * i / 40;
        env.push([w, m.tau(w) * 1000]);
      }
      p.band(env, 0, { fill: "var(--s2)", opacity: 0.12 });
      p.path(env, { stroke: "var(--s2)", width: 2.5 });
      p.dot(wCorner, tLim, { fill: "var(--s2)" });
      p.tag(wCorner, tLim, "corner " + fmt(wCorner, 0) + " rad/s", "var(--s2)", "start", 9, -8);
      p.tag(Math.max(0, wTop), state.yMax, "ideal line: " + fmt(m.tStall * 1000, 0) +
            " mN·m at stall", "var(--s1)", "end", -9, 15);
      p.tag(0, tCon, "continuous " + state.con + " A", "var(--critical)", "start", 6, -6);

      sEls[0].textContent = fmt(tLim, 0);
      sEls[1].textContent = fmt(wCorner, 0);
      sEls[2].textContent = fmt(state.lim * state.lim * R_DEF, 1);
      sEls[3].textContent = fmt(state.con * state.con * R_DEF, 1);
    }
    sLim.r.addEventListener("input", draw);
    sCon.r.addEventListener("input", draw);
    draw();

    host.appendChild(legend([
      { c: "var(--s2)", t: "Usable envelope" },
      { c: "var(--s1)", t: "Ideal line (unlimited current)", dash: true },
      { c: "var(--critical)", t: "Above continuous rating" }
    ]));
    attachHover(host, [p], function (w) {
      var tIdeal = m.tau(w) * 1000, tLim = KT * state.lim * 1000;
      var t = Math.min(tIdeal, tLim);
      if (t < 0) return "<b>" + fmt(w, 0) + " rad/s</b><br>beyond no-load speed";
      var I = t / 1000 / KT;
      return "<b>" + fmt(w, 0) + " rad/s</b><br>Torque " + fmt(t, 0) + " mN·m<br>Current " +
             fmt(I, 1) + " A<br>Copper loss " + fmt(I * I * R_DEF, 1) + " W" +
             (I > state.con ? "<br><b>above continuous</b>" : "");
    });
    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-note",
      "Copper loss is I<sup>2</sup>R, so the two loss readouts move apart much faster than the " +
      "two currents do. That is the whole argument of this section in one pair of numbers: " +
      "double the current and you quadruple the heat."));
  })();

  // ==================================================== 4. AS2303 measured
  (function () {
    var host = document.getElementById("viz-as2303");
    if (!host) return;

    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-title", "AS2303 — measured against model"));

    if (!MEASURED.length) {
      host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-sub",
        "Placeholder. The model line below is drawn from the datasheet k<sub>V</sub> and a " +
        "placeholder winding resistance; no bench data has been loaded yet."));
      var m0 = model(U_DEF, R_DEF), ny0 = niceUp(m0.tStall * 1000, 4);
      var p0 = Panel(host, { height: 230, xDomain: [0, m0.w0], yDomain: [0, ny0.top],
                             aria: "Model torque-speed line, awaiting measured data" });
      p0.axes(niceIn(m0.w0, 5), ny0.ticks, "Shaft speed ω [rad/s]", "Torque [mN·m]");
      p0.path([[0, m0.tStall * 1000], [m0.w0, 0]],
              { stroke: "var(--muted)", width: 2, dash: "6 5" });
      host.appendChild(html("div", "viz-empty",
        "<b>No test-stand data loaded.</b><br>Paste the measured operating points into the " +
        "<code>MEASURED</code> array at the top of the script block in " +
        "<code>reference/bldc.qmd</code>. Each row is <code>{ w, tau, I }</code> — speed in " +
        "rad/s, torque in mN·m, DC current in amps. The plot switches to a " +
        "measured-versus-model comparison automatically, and the fitted resistance appears " +
        "below it."));
      return;
    }

    host.appendChild(html("p", "viz-sub",
      "Points are test-stand measurements; the dashed line is the ideal model. Divergence at " +
      "the low-speed end is where the straight-line assumption gives out."));
    var wMax = Math.max.apply(null, MEASURED.map(function (d) { return d.w; }));
    var tMax = Math.max.apply(null, MEASURED.map(function (d) { return d.tau; }));
    var m = model(U_DEF, R_DEF);
    var xMax = Math.max(wMax * 1.05, m.w0);
    var nyM = niceUp(Math.max(tMax * 1.15, KT * 30 * 1000), 4);
    var p = Panel(host, { height: 250, xDomain: [0, xMax], yDomain: [0, nyM.top],
                          aria: "Measured torque against speed compared with the model" });
    p.axes(niceIn(xMax, 5), nyM.ticks, "Shaft speed ω [rad/s]", "Torque [mN·m]");
    p.path([[0, m.tStall * 1000], [m.w0, 0]], { stroke: "var(--s1)", width: 2, dash: "5 4" });
    MEASURED.forEach(function (d) { p.dot(d.w, d.tau, { fill: "var(--s2)", r: 4.5 }); });
    host.appendChild(legend([
      { c: "var(--s2)", t: "Measured" },
      { c: "var(--s1)", t: "Model", dash: true }
    ]));
    table(host, ["ω [rad/s]", "Torque [mN·m]", "Current [A]"],
      MEASURED.map(function (d) {
        return [fmt(d.w, 0), fmt(d.tau, 1), d.I === undefined ? "—" : fmt(d.I, 1)];
      }));
  })();
})();
</script>

:::
